title: What Is an Agent Registry?
summary: A registry only counts if something checks it before access is granted. What each entry has to hold, what MCP, A2A and Entra Agent ID actually record, and what regulators already make you register.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


**A registry earns the name only when something refuses an agent that has no entry. Most of what ships under the name is a searchable list with an owner column.**


The list part is now commodity. Microsoft's Agent 365 registry opens on three counters: total agents, agents without owners, and unmanaged agents, that last one defined as agents "created or managed outside of Agent 365, without its risk protection and observability."


The usual plan treats the record as the hard part and enforcement as a later phase. We think it is the other way round. Writing down an owner, a purpose and a scope takes an afternoon. Getting a gateway, an identity provider and an MCP server to agree on what happens when an unregistered agent calls is the part that changes anything.


None of that makes documentation worthless. A registry with no teeth still answers audit questions, and Article 49 of the EU AI Act makes registration a legal act for some systems no matter what you enforce.


So start from the enforcement point you already own. Find the hop every agent call passes through, make it require a registry identifier, and let the record grow into whatever that hop needs in order to decide.
